text:
Samuel Girard came to Pittsburgh as a puck mover, and the puck moving is still there. What's missing is the payoff. He has seven points in 15 games playing 19 minutes a night, but he's now pointless in seven straight, and the chances have thinned out too, so this isn't just bad luck.

Some of it is, though. With Girard on the ice the Penguins have scored 8.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve, which is a lot of lost assists for a defenceman whose game is feeding teammates. He's at 51% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances), which is fine on a team in the state Pittsburgh is in. Evolving-Hockey had him at 1.7 wins above replacement last season, 34th among defencemen, with the caveat that he played beside strong teammates in Colorado. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking calls him a setup man: 5.9 primary shot assists per 60, 86th percentile among defencemen. Watch that number. When his teammates' shots start going in again, his points come back in bunches.
